A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same RoboMaster paper with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–C. Pages 2–19 are textually and visually identical; differences are confined to first-page author information and the arXiv stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original Bridge V2 evaluations, baseline comparisons, user-preference results, and ablations in Tables 2–6, plus qualitative generation results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original quantitative experiments, ablations, user-preference results, and supplementary qualitative results.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Table R7 retain the same interaction-phase decomposition, appearance/shape embeddings, causal feature propagation, motion injector, architecture, and training objective.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Bridge V2 coverage and in-the-wild manipulation examples. Appendix C retains the same out-of-domain objects, manipulation skills, and autoregressive long-video scenarios.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain IRASim, MotionCtrl, DragAnything, and Tora. Figures 5–6 retain the same comparisons with Tora and DragAnything; no comparator membership changes.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 and Appendix A preserve the same data preparation, 214-sample test set, CogVideoX-5B configuration, 480×640 resolution, 37-frame videos, training/inference settings, and evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: Tables 4–6 retain identical component ablations, mask-sparsity tests, and trajectory-perturbation tests. The accompanying visual analyses and supplementary generalization examples are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative examples match. For example, Table 2 reports RoboMaster FVD 147.31, robot/object trajectory errors 16.47/24.16, and user preference 47.33% in both versions.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(7), including the task definition, embeddings, conditional factorization, motion injection, and loss, are identical. The appendices introduce no changed mathematical definitions, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about collaborative trajectory control, object awareness, easier user annotation, and state-of-the-art robotic-manipulation video generation.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning feature entanglement and object identity are unchanged. Section 5 retains the same limitations involving out-of-domain distortions, 2D control, and generalization across robot embodiments.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A preserve the same hardware, hyperparameters, data-curation pipeline, annotation instructions, and network details. The project-page access information is also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix B, and all 69 reference entries are identical, preserving the same research positioning and relationships to earlier methods.

P1.justification: v2 removes Xiao Fu's internship marker and the footnote stating that the work was done during an internship at KwaiVGI, Kuaishou Technology. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; scientific prose and document organization remain identical.

P2.justification: The first-page author text shifts slightly and its footnote becomes shorter. All figures, tables, captions, and their placement remain unchanged, with pages 2–19 rendering identically.

improvement.justification: v2 changes only first-page author-footnote information, minor spacing, and version metadata. The method, evidence, explanations, limitations, and appendices are identical, so these limited edits do not materially change overall paper quality.
